Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with reported head
impact and immediate post-traumatic symptoms consistent with concussion. The mechanism
of injury and the force involved are well matched to the injuries described at intake.
Neurological examination and imaging findings clearly confirm the diagnosis of
concussion with post-concussive symptoms including headache, dizziness, light
sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating. Patient has no known prior injury to the
head or neck. Care was delivered over 27 visits, which is somewhat longer than typical
for this injury, with gradual progression through vestibular therapy, graded return to
activity, and symptom monitoring. Symptoms improved steadily over the course of care,
though recovery was slower in the later weeks. Billing records reflect single charges
for each service rendered, with no duplicate or repeated billing entries. Patient is
currently improving and is expected to continue a home exercise program with follow-up
as needed.

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
